title: Spinach and Ricotta Cannelloni
subtitle: Filled pasta tubes baked in tomato sauce with mozzarella
excerpt: Pasta sheets rolled around a creamy spinach and ricotta filling, baked in a simple tomato sauce and covered with melted mozzarella. A classic Italian baked pasta that feeds a crowd.
sourceNotes: Cannelloni is a baked pasta from central and southern Italy. The spinach and ricotta filling became the most popular version across Italy and abroad during the 20th century.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to a day ahead. Cover and refrigerate. Add 10 minutes to the bake time from cold.

content.text: Squeeze as much water as possible from the wilted spinach; excess moisture makes the filling slack and the pasta soggy.

items.prepNote: wilted in a hot dry pan, then squeezed dry and roughly chopped

content.text: For the sauce, heat the olive oil in the saucepan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tinned tomatoes and crush with a spoon. Season and simmer for 10 minutes. Stir in the basil.
For the filling, mix the ricotta, squeezed spinach, most of the parmesan, the egg, and nutmeg in a bowl. Season well.
Spoon the filling into a piping bag or a zip-lock bag with one corner snipped off.
Pipe the filling into each cannelloni tube, filling generously from both ends.
Spread half the tomato sauce over the base of the baking dish.
Arrange the filled tubes in a single layer on top.
Spoon the remaining sauce over. Scatter with mozzarella and the remaining parmesan.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until bubbling and golden on top. Leave to rest for 5 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: Pasta tubes are still firm after baking.
items.cause: Not enough sauce covering the tubes during cooking.
items.fix: Add a splash of water to the dish, cover with foil, bake 10 more minutes.

items.cause: Spinach was not squeezed dry enough.
items.fix: Wring it in a clean cloth next time; there should be no drips.

items.symptom: Top is burning before pasta is cooked.
items.cause: Oven temperature too high or dish too close to the top element.
items.fix: Cover loosely with foil for the remaining cooking time.
